funders.title: Who funds the Foundation
funders.globalIntro: The Rotary Foundation’s donor base is 76.1% individuals — 478,629 people gave in 2024–25. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation is its giant partner on polio, governments fund the wider eradication effort, and clubs worldwide do the rest.
funders.countriesNote: Top 10 giving countries, all TRF funds, 2024–25 (per-capita = Annual Fund per Rotarian). The US figure includes a $100M PolioPlus gift from the Gates Foundation.

gates.title: The Gates Foundation
gates.text: Rotary’s match partner since 2007: every dollar Rotary commits to polio is matched two-to-one. The June 2025 renewal is a joint commitment of up to $450M over three years (Rotary raises $50M a year, Gates adds two). Cumulatively the Gates Foundation has put $6.18B into the GPEI — its largest private donor.

donorBase.title: The real base: Rotarians themselves
donorBase.text: In 2024–25: 4 donors gave $1M+ ($12.2M), 51 gave $250K+, 1,604 gave $10K+, and 45,121 passed the $1,000 Paul Harris Fellow mark. 87.2% of all 35,633 clubs gave something — including 156 districts where every single club participated.

funders.districtTitle: In our district — D9212’s legacy, Kenya’s giants
funders.districtIntro: The Rotary Foundation does not publish per-district donor ledgers — but the district’s own farewell conference decks do. The tables below come from the giving records presented at the D9212 send-off, alongside the names confirmed in public records.

districtNamed.name: Geeta & Kaushik Manek
districtNamed.detail: Rotary Club of Muthaiga. Arch Klumph Society members, Major Donors, Benefactors and Bequest Society members. Geeta was the first female Governor of District 9200 (2013–14), served as a Trustee of The Rotary Foundation — chairing its Executive, Programs and Stewardship committees — and received Rotary’s Service Above Self Award. Kaushik led District 9200 as Governor in 2008–09.

districtNamed.name: Dr. Manu Chandaria
districtNamed.detail: Rotary Club of Nairobi — Kenya’s Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy laureate (2022). The visionary and financial backbone of the Kenya Rural Blindness Eradication Project (the 17,000-surgery story is in the achievements below).

districtClubs.title: Top five giving clubs — the full thirteen years
districtClubs.intro: Cumulative TRF giving across District 9212’s thirteen-year life, as honored at the district’s farewell.
districtClubs.note: All five are Nairobi-area clubs — and our own club sits fourth all-time at nearly a quarter of a million dollars.

lastDance.title: 2025/26 giving leaderboard — “the last dance”
lastDance.intro: The final Rotary year of District 9212, as presented at the farewell: the top twenty giving clubs.
lastDance.note: Muthaiga led the last dance, and all four all-time top clubs stayed in the year’s top four — with Kitengela, whose African-culture fashion show raised polio money, finishing fifth.

heritage.title: Heritage clubs — our enduring roots
heritage.intro: The fourteen oldest clubs of the district, in order of charter — the roots every D9212 club grew from.
heritage.note: Our club is the sixth-oldest in the lineage — chartered in 1963, the same year as Kisumu.

legacyStory.title: The Sunshine Rally — one man’s compassion, thousands of smiles
legacyStory.text: In 1979, Dr. Manu Chandaria — renowned industrialist, philanthropist and past president of the Rotary Club of Nairobi — began the Rotary Sunshine Rally: a joyful day in the sun for children living with disabilities, built on laughter, dignity, love and belonging, at a time when conversations around inclusion were still limited. In 1980–81, during the UN International Year for the Handicapped and Rotary’s 75th anniversary, clubs across Nairobi, Kiambu, Thika and Machakos officially adopted it. What began as a local act of kindness is today one of Kenya’s most enduring humanitarian legacies.

districtAggregate: District 9212’s TRF giving: ~$290,000 in 2022–23 (against a $400K goal), with a $500,000 target for 2025–26 and a $1M+ three-year ambition.
Kenya sits at the doorstep of the global top 30 — Nepal holds #30 at ~$450K. Meeting the 2025–26 target puts Kenyan giving inside that table.
Signature fundraisers: RC Lavington’s award-winning End Polio Bikeathon, Foundation dinners across Kenya, Ethiopia and South Sudan, and first-of-their-kind district art exhibitions.

polio.title: PolioPlus: the promise
polio.intro: 1985: Rotary pledges to immunize every child on Earth. 1988: Rotary co-founds the GPEI with WHO, UNICEF and the CDC (Gates and Gavi join later). The finish line is now in sight — and every matched dollar pushes the last mile.
polio.caseNote: Wild poliovirus cases per year, all countries. Africa was certified wild-polio-free in 2020. 2026 counts: 22 through August.
polio.kenyaTitle: Kenya & District 9212 in the polio story
kenya: District 9212 partnered with Kenya’s Ministry of Health, WHO, UNICEF and the Gates Foundation for five-county immunization campaigns — Migori, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Narok and Siaya — with the official launch hosted in Migori.

End Polio walks ran nationwide: Nairobi (University of Nairobi graduation square), Mombasa, Naivasha, Taveta, Mwatate, Voi, Nyeri, Thika and Suna — plus 100-day giving campaigns by RC Hurlingham (KSh 600K target) and RC Nairobi Kilimani Alfajiri’s gold/silver/bronze daily tiers.

Immunization drives RCNS helped organize include the Kikopey campaign with RC Hurlingham, Ngong Road, Nairobi East, Milimani and Parklands — and the St. Catherine Primary School drive in Nairobi’s South B.
Trustee Geeta Manek and Dr. David Githanga carried the district’s polio message onto national television talk shows for World Polio Day.

achievementsGlobal.title: Co-founding the polio endgame
achievementsGlobal.detail: PolioPlus and the GPEI — a volunteer organization promised a world without polio, and the world’s health agencies followed. The full story is the polio section.

achievementsGlobal.title: 99.9% of wild polio eliminated
achievementsGlobal.detail: The steepest disease decline in public-health history — charted above.

achievementsGlobal.title: Africa certified wild-polio-free
achievementsGlobal.detail: Four years with zero wild poliovirus across the African region — Kenya’s immunization drives in the vanguard.

achievementsGlobal.title: The Gates 2:1 match
achievementsGlobal.detail: The partnership that triples every Rotary polio dollar — the funding engine of the endgame (details in the funders section).

achievementsGlobal.title: $7.2B contributed since 1917
achievementsGlobal.detail: Klumph’s seed idea, compounding for a century — 2024–25 set the all-time record.

achievementsGlobal.title: A $2.05B permanent endowment
achievementsGlobal.detail: The 2025-by-2025 campaign beat its own target — principal untouched, earnings funding programs forever.

achievementsGlobal.title: 17 straight 4-star ratings
achievementsGlobal.detail: Charity Navigator’s top rating every year since 2009 — scored 99/100.

achievementsGlobal.title: Eight Rotary Peace Centers
achievementsGlobal.detail: Capacity rises to 170 fellowships a year with the new Symbiosis center (Pune, 2026); Africa’s first was Makerere (2021).

achievementsGlobal.title: Programs of Scale — five $2M awards
achievementsGlobal.detail: Malaria-free Zambia (1.2M people, 2,500 health workers) · healthy families Nigeria · cervical cancer Egypt (30K girls vaccinated, 4M reached) · water & harvests India (60K farmers, +25–30% income) · peace Colombia ($3M with the World Food Programme).

achievementsGlobal.title: The 2024–25 grant engine
achievementsGlobal.detail: 1,423 global grants ($81.0M), 468 district grants ($27.8M), 74 disaster response grants ($1.9M) — one year’s output of the SHARE engine.

achievementsGlobal.title: Advocacy that moved governments
achievementsGlobal.detail: Rotary’s advocacy has unlocked more than $21B in government funding for polio eradication — including Saudi Arabia’s $500M pledge in 2024.

achievementsGlobal.title: A giving culture without equal
achievementsGlobal.detail: Nearly four in ten Rotarians give in a typical year — a participation culture few charities match.

achievementsGlobal.title: Scholarships and peace fellowships
achievementsGlobal.detail: $5.2M invested in fellows and centers in 2024–25 alone; global grants also fund graduate scholarships and vocational training teams.

achievementsGlobal.title: Digital-era fundraising
achievementsGlobal.detail: Donor engagement campaigns generated $41.7M (+8% YoY); Raise for Rotary peer events raised $2.7M from 18,500 donors in 140+ countries.

achievementsGlobal.title: The environment becomes cause #7
achievementsGlobal.detail: Supporting the Environment joined the areas of focus — Rotary’s youngest cause.

achievementsDistrict.title: 17,000+ free eye surgeries
achievementsDistrict.detail: The Kenya Rural Blindness Eradication Project: Dr. Manu Chandaria and RC Nairobi, backed by 50 clubs from Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium. Camps at Kapkatet and Kabarak — one performed 309 cataract surgeries with President Moi in attendance; the programme ran nine years.

achievementsDistrict.title: The Sunshine Rally begins
achievementsDistrict.detail: Dr. Manu Chandaria’s day in the sun for children living with disabilities — the full story is in the funders section.

achievementsDistrict.title: RCNS’s Jaipur Foot Project
achievementsDistrict.detail: Our club founded the prosthetics programme that became the Jaipur Foot Trust — restoring mobility to thousands of amputees.

achievementsDistrict.title: RCNS’s National Sanitary Pads Campaign
achievementsDistrict.detail: Launched with the Girl Child Network (President Megan White, Rtn. Naisiae Paloshe) — it grew into the national Sanitary Towels Campaign and a government programme keeping girls in school.

achievementsDistrict.title: Polio campaigns across five counties
achievementsDistrict.detail: Migori, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Narok and Siaya, with the Ministry of Health, WHO, UNICEF and the Gates Foundation — RCNS co-organized the Kikopey drive (full story in the polio section).

achievementsDistrict.title: District polio giving doubled
achievementsDistrict.detail: $36,885 in 2023–24 to $72,857 in 2024–25 — walk by walk, shilling by shilling.

achievementsDistrict.title: Geeta Manek on the global board
achievementsDistrict.detail: The district’s voice at the Foundation’s highest table — full profile in the funders section above.

achievementsDistrict.title: Rotary born in East Africa
achievementsDistrict.detail: RC Nairobi — chartered 11 March 1930 at the New Stanley Hotel by John Innes and Mayor Charles Udall — Africa’s third-oldest club and the root of every East African club; Juba joined the family in 2010.

achievementsDistrict.title: RCNS — 63 years of service
achievementsDistrict.detail: Chartered 1963 (second-oldest Nairobi club, third in Kenya); Golden Jubilee in June 2013 graced by First Lady Margaret Kenyatta.

achievementsDistrict.title: Best TRF Giving Club in the district
achievementsDistrict.detail: RCNS won the coveted Foundation giving award at the 91st District Conference in Addis Ababa.

achievementsDistrict.title: Africa’s first eco-club
achievementsDistrict.detail: RC Lavington Eco — the continent’s first environment-focused Rotary club — chartered under Wairimu Njage (RC Lavington).

achievementsDistrict.title: First-of-its-kind district art exhibitions
achievementsDistrict.detail: Kenya and Ethiopia hosted joint exhibitions around Darren Jones’s “Imagine Ones Dream” — $115K+ raised for under-five immunization and surveillance.

achievementsDistrict.title: A district that outgrew itself
achievementsDistrict.detail: D9212 spanned four countries and grew to 267 clubs and 3,727 Rotarians — 90% of clubs voted to split, and 101 District Conferences closed the story at Naivasha in 2026.

achievementsDistrict.title: The next chapter: D9215 & D9216
achievementsDistrict.detail: From 1 July 2026, D9215 (Western Kenya, Rift Valley, Western Nairobi + South Sudan) and D9216 (Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central & Eastern Kenya, Coast) carry the flag — RCNS serves in D9215.

achievementsDistrict.title: RCNS builds the next generation
achievementsDistrict.detail: Our club chartered RC Kirinyaga, mentors Rotaract Kenyatta University (100+ members) and Interact clubs at State House Girls and Upper Hill — and sponsors 30 needy students through secondary school.

club.title: Our club & the Foundation
club.intro: The Rotary Foundation story has a Nairobi South thread running through it — highlighted wherever it appears on this page.
items: Chartered 1963 — look for our highlighted rows above: fourth on the all-time giving table, sixth in the heritage lineage.
Our stories above: the Jaipur Foot Project, the national pads campaign, the Kikopey drive and the district’s Best TRF Giving Club award — each tagged in the district achievements.
